object.description: Matter tells spacetime how to curve, and curved spacetime tells matter how to move. The left side is the geometry of spacetime, the right its content of matter and energy; the line stands for ten coupled equations. Einstein presented them to the Prussian Academy of Sciences in Berlin on 25 November 1915, after eight years of work and a final month of racing David Hilbert. They replaced Newton's law a few rows back, and they describe black holes, the expanding universe and the gravitational waves first heard a century later.
facts: Karl Schwarzschild found the first exact solution, the one that describes a black hole, within weeks, while serving in the German army on the Russian front; he died in 1916.
The 1919 solar eclipse expeditions led by Arthur Eddington measured the bending of starlight the equations predict and made Einstein famous overnight.
In 1917 Einstein added a cosmological constant to keep the universe static; it was dropped when Hubble found the expansion, and brought back in 1998 for dark energy.
